plan.topic: Tirzepatide vs dulaglutide in heart failure: exploratory SURPASS-CVOT analysis in adults with type 2 diabetes, heart disease and a history of heart failure
plan.angle:
Title: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) vs Dulaglutide (Trulicity) in Heart Failure: What Did the Trial Find?'

Answer by 10 s: 'An early signal, not proof. In adults with type 2 diabetes, heart disease and a history of heart failure, death or a heart-failure hospital visit happened in 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide over about 4 years. Heart-failure hospital visits on their own were about the same.'

Then:
- Explain it's a post hoc look at SURPASS-CVOT (13,299 adults, so about 2,700 with heart failure; per-arm sizes from the EJPC paper). The comparison is dulaglutide, not placebo, and the authors call it hypothesis-generating.
- Status: as of Oct 2026, tirzepatide isn't FDA-approved to treat heart failure.
- One line on GI side effects.
- 'Don't switch or stop on your own.'
- Prescriber line.

On screen: 'post hoc analysis · SURPASS-CVOT · vs dulaglutide, not placebo · HF hospital visits alone: no clear difference'. Keep 'linked to' or 'associated with' language. 170 words or fewer, no emoji.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) vs Dulaglutide (Trulicity): Fewer Heart-Failure Events?
plan.why:
Head-to-heads that name both drugs, with tirzepatide first, are our strongest YouTube pattern (SURMOUNT-5 147), and almost no creators have covered this yet. | fact-check: I confirmed the figures. The primary source is 'Outcomes in patients with diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and heart failure treated with tirzepatide or dulaglutide: SURPASS-CVOT analysis', European Journal of Preventive Cardiology, Oct 15, 2026. About 20.3% of the 13,299 participants (about 2,698 people) had a self-reported history of heart failure. Follow-up averaged about 4 years. All-cause death or heart-failure hospitalization/urgent visit: 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70–0.99). The authors call this composite post hoc, 'hypothesis generating' and 'nominal', with no adjustment for multiple comparisons.

The framing problem: the result is driven by death. All-cause death was 13.5% vs 16.7%. Heart-failure hospitalization or urgent visit alone did not differ (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.73–1.27, Healio/Endocrine Today, Jan 2026). CV death or HF events was HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.70–1.03), also not significant. A Heart Failure Reviews editorial called it 'a tie'. So the working title 'Fewer Heart-Failure Events?', and the line 'death or heart-failure events', imply something the analysis didn't show.

The angle also mixes up 'exploratory subgroup' and 'post hoc'. Here the subgroup was prespecified but the endpoint was post hoc.

Get the per-arm subgroup sizes from the EJPC paper itself. AJMC doesn't give them.

Sources checked: AJMC (https://www.ajmc.com/view/tirzepatide-linked-to-lower-death-or-hf-event-rates-in-t2d-hf, used only to locate the paper) and Healio (https://www.healio.com/news/endocrinology/20260120/tirzepatide-heart-effects-do-not-vary-by-heart-failure-status).

package.description:
Tirzepatide vs dulaglutide in about 2,700 adults with type 2 diabetes, heart or blood-vessel disease and self-reported past heart failure (SURPASS-CVOT, about 4 years): death or a heart-failure hospital/urgent visit 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide; heart-failure visits alone 7.6% vs 7.7%, no clear difference. Exploratory, hypothesis-generating subgroup. Tirzepatide isn't FDA-approved for heart failure as of October 2026. Nausea and diarrhea are common.

• Death or a heart-failure hospital/urgent visit: 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide

factcheck.summary:
I checked every number against the primary paper (Nicholls SJ et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol, online Oct 15, 2026) and the AJMC report.

**The figures all match the sources:**
- Of 13,299 randomized adults, 2,678 (20.3%) had heart-failure history, and that history was self-reported.
- The tables line up exactly:
  - Death or heart-failure events: 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide (HR 0.83, 0.70–0.99).
  - Death from any cause: 13.5% vs 16.7% (HR 0.80).
  - Heart-failure hospital or urgent visits alone: 7.6% vs 7.7% (HR 0.97, 0.73–1.27).
  - Heart death or heart-failure events: HR 0.85 (0.70–1.03), not significant.
- Average follow-up was about 4 years.
- The paper confirms there was no multiplicity adjustment and uses the words "exploratory" and "hypothesis-generating".

**Sources and status:**
- Healio (Dec 2, 2025) confirms the AHA 2025 presentation: the benefit came from fatal events, with no difference in non-fatal heart-failure outcomes. That supports its tag on s3, although Healio doesn't print the 7.6%/7.7% figures; the paper and AJMC cover those.
- The status line is accurate. Tirzepatide is approved for type 2 diabetes, weight management and sleep apnea, but not heart failure. Lilly withdrew its HFpEF application in 2025.
- Both Lilly label PDFs load, but I couldn't read the text inside them. I'm leaving them in the list because the status line was confirmed separately and "nausea and diarrhea are common" is standard tirzepatide label wording.

**Script quality:** The framing is careful: "early signal, not proof", absolute rates next to each drug, an active comparator rather than placebo, and the no-difference result on heart-failure visits shown clearly. The narration is about 167 words, the hook pays off, and the dated status, a common side effect and the prescriber line are all there.

**What's left:** Three wording fixes, all minor. The big one is to give the group sizes per arm instead of the combined subgroup number, as the craft rules require.

issues.claim: "This was a subgroup of about 2,700 of 13,299 randomized adults who self-reported past heart failure"
issues.problem: The craft rule is to give group sizes per arm, never a combined N. The paper reports 1,310 on tirzepatide and 1,368 on dulaglutide (2,678 total). The fix also keeps the word count under 170 (about 168).
issues.fix: Narration: "This was a subgroup: 1,310 adults on tirzepatide and 1,368 on dulaglutide who self-reported past heart failure, out of 13,299 randomized, and the results weren't adjusted for multiple comparisons." items[1]: "Self-reported past heart failure: 1,310 on tirzepatide vs 1,368 on dulaglutide (of 13,299 randomized)"

issues.problem: The narration and items say "HF hospital or urgent visits alone". The screen text drops "alone" and the drug pairing, so it reads broader than the narration.

issues.claim: publisher "Healio / Endocrine Today, online Dec 2, 2025" with a URL path dated 20260120
issues.problem: The page shows Dec 2, 2025, but the URL path is dated Jan 20, 2026 (likely a print or reissue date). Healio also doesn't print the 7.6%/7.7% figures; it only supports "no difference in non-fatal heart-failure outcomes".
issues.fix: Set publisher to "Healio / Endocrine Today, online Dec 2, 2025 (URL dated Jan 20, 2026)". Keep src3 on s3 only for the no-difference statement; the numbers come from src1 and src2.

notes: Caption card 'TIRZEPATIDE VERSUS DULAGLUTIDE,' ends on a trailing comma instead of a complete clause.
Caption card 'FIRST, THIS IS AN EARLY' ends on the bare article+adjective 'AN EARLY', splitting the phrase 'an early trial/signal'.
Caption '2 DIABETES,' ends on a comma and reads as a stray fragment of 'Type 2 diabetes'.
Next card 'AND SELF-REPORTED PAST' ends on the bare adjective 'PAST', splitting the fixed phrase 'past heart failure' across cards.
'HOSPITAL OR URGENT VISIT,' ends on a comma.
'THAT'S OVER ABOUT' ends on the preposition 'ABOUT'.
Numbers are spelled out and split across cards ('CAUSE WERE THIRTEEN' then 'VERSUS SIXTEEN POINT'), contradicting the on-screen numerals 13.5% vs 16.7%.
'VERSUS SIXTEEN POINT' ends on the bare word 'POINT'.
'BUT HERE'S THE THING:' is a filler cliché ending on a colon.
'POINT SEVEN PERCENT.' continues a spelled-out, split number for 7.6% vs 7.7%.
'AND THE COMBINED' ends on the bare adjective 'COMBINED'.
'NOW, SURPASS-CVOT WASN'T DESIGNED' ends on the verb 'DESIGNED', splitting the phrase 'wasn't designed to study heart failure'.
'THIS WAS A SUBGROUP,' ends on a comma.
Stat pill '~2,700 of 13,299' and its subtitle sit on top of the hero character group (confirmed by automated on-hero finding) at both 59.6s and 68.3s.
Caption 'ABOUT TWENTY-SEVEN HUNDRED' spells out the number instead of using the on-screen numeral '~2,700'.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits well under speech already (-13.5dB) so only a small -1.4dB overall trim to tame an over-loud pause swell (-10.4 vs ~-14 target); can't fully fix the pause level without the under-voice bed dropping out of range, so it's a partial correction. Rebalanced a handful of outlier cues: boosted an under-heard pause transition (swell/tick at 28.6s), pulled down a stray loud swoosh during the serious "not a heart-failure trial" caveat and a couple of other speech-bed cues that crept above -14dB, and trimmed one redundant bubble and blip from two overcrowded reveal clusters. Added three bespoke, low-key accents (heartbeat for the heart-disease label, a soft caution chime for "Not FDA-Approved", a warm chime for the closing prescriber line) to add polish without competing with the narration.
